VECC.name: Kolkata / Dum Dum
VECC.geo: On the Hooghly, gateway to eastern India.
VECC.av: Scheduled traffic from 1924. KLM stopped here on Amsterdam–Batavia. Imperial used Calcutta on London–Australia from 1933. Earhart stopped June 1937.
VECC.line: Dum Dum. In the 1930s this grass was a stop on the Europe–Australia trunk.
VECC.why: Monsoon and river fog. Carry the reserve you calculated.

VEAB.name: Prayagraj (Allahabad)
VEAB.av: 18 Feb 1911: Henri Pequet flew Allahabad→Naini, about 6 miles / 9.7 km, 6,500 letters — first official airmail flight.
VEAB.line: Allahabad. Six miles and a bag of letters started civil flying in India.

NAINI.name: Naini
NAINI.geo: Just across the Yamuna from Allahabad.
NAINI.av: Landing end of the 18 Feb 1911 airmail hop.
NAINI.line: Naini. The world's first official airmail ended in this field.
NAINI.why: Short hop. See the whole distance on the side view.

VAAH.name: Ahmedabad
VAAH.geo: Sabarmati river. Desert to the west, coast to the south.
VAAH.av: Stop on J.R.D. Tata's 15 Oct 1932 Karachi–Bombay mail flight.
VAAH.line: Ahmedabad. Tata put the Puss Moth down here on the first Tata mail day.
VAAH.why: A fuel stop turns one long desert leg into two safe ones.

VAJJ.name: Mumbai / Juhu
VAJJ.geo: Island city on the Arabian Sea.
VAJJ.av: Juhu aerodrome 1928. 15 Oct 1932 Tata landed a Puss Moth here from Karachi via Ahmedabad.
VAJJ.line: Juhu beach strip. Tata's 1932 mail run ended on this sand.

VIDP.name: Delhi
VIDP.av: Dec 1912: first international service into India, London–Karachi–Delhi.
VIDP.line: Delhi. The first international air service into India aimed at this city in 1912.
VIDP.why: Winter fog. Hold or divert — that is an ETA problem.

VEBD.name: Bagdogra
VEBD.geo: Siliguri corridor. Plains under the first wall of the Himalaya.
VEBD.av: 21 May 1927: Bengal Air Transport flew cargo Calcutta–Bagdogra.
VEBD.line: Bagdogra. Tea gardens below, mountains ahead.

VNKT.name: Kathmandu
VNKT.av: Mountain-gate field. Thin air is the lesson.
VNKT.line: Kathmandu valley. Thin air — the wing has less to bite.
VNKT.why: Density altitude. Same indicated speed, less lift.

OPKC.name: Karachi
OPKC.geo: Arabian Sea. Western door of South Asia.
OPKC.av: Western end of the 1932 Tata mail run and Imperial's India service.
OPKC.line: Karachi. Where Europe's air route used to hand India the mail.
OPKC.why: Desert heat and a sea breeze near the coast.

EGCR.name: London Croydon
EGCR.av: London's main civil airport from 29 Mar 1920 after Hounslow. Terminal 1928. Closed 1959.
EGCR.line: Croydon was London's door to Paris and to India.
EGCR.why: Tight airspace. Heading is not a suggestion.

EGLL.name: London Heathrow
EGLL.line: Heathrow. The field that replaced Croydon.
EGLL.why: Crowded. Fly the number you planned.

LFPB.name: Paris Le Bourget
LFPB.av: Civil from 1919. Lindbergh landed Spirit of St. Louis here 21 May 1927.
LFPB.line: Le Bourget. Lindbergh's Atlantic ended on this grass in 1927.
LFPB.why: Short European hop. Good ETA practice.

EDDK.name: Cologne
EDDK.av: Imperial London–Brussels–Cologne 3 May 1924. India mail turned here 2 Nov 1929.
EDDK.line: Cologne. In 1929 the India mail turned here for Vienna.

EDDN.name: Nuremberg
EDDN.av: Stop on Imperial's 2 Nov 1929 routing between Cologne and Vienna.
EDDN.line: Nuremberg. Next bead after Cologne on the 1929 mail string.

LOWW.name: Vienna
LOWW.av: On Imperial's Nov 1929 central-Europe mail routing.
LOWW.line: Vienna. Mail to India once came through this city by air.

LHBP.name: Budapest
LHBP.av: On the 1929 mail string. Ferihegy civil from May 1950.
LHBP.line: Budapest. The 1929 India mail crossed the Danube here.

EGHI.name: Southampton / Calshot
EGHI.av: Calshot 1913. Empire flying boats from March 1937.
EGHI.line: Southampton Water. The Empire boats left this inlet in 1937.
EGHI.why: Water chapter. Side view shows a hull.

LFML.name: Marseille
LFML.av: On later Empire / flying-boat routings toward Italy.
LFML.line: Marseille. France's south door onto the Middle Sea.

LIRN.name: Naples
LIRN.geo: Bay of Naples. Vesuvius on the side view.
LIRN.line: Naples. Volcano on the right, bay under the nose.
LIRN.why: The mountain is a wind machine.

LIBR.name: Brindisi
LIBR.av: Imperial passengers often trained to Brindisi, then boat to Athens.
LIBR.line: Brindisi. Where the train handed the Empire route back to a boat.
LIBR.why: Sea breeze and a long water fetch.

LGAV.name: Athens
LGAV.geo: Attica. First glimpse of the Aegean.
LGAV.av: Stop on Imperial's eastbound Empire routing. Last European land on Chapter 10.
LGAV.line: Athens. After this the old Empire route left Europe.
LGAV.why: Last European land before the corridor.

EIDW.name: Dublin
EIDW.av: Opened 19 January 1942. Aer Lingus to Shannon Aug 1942.
EIDW.line: Dublin. Opened in 1942; the short sea hop to Britain starts here.
EIDW.why: A westerly is a gift going home, a tax going out.

EINN.name: Shannon / Foynes
EINN.geo: Shannon estuary. Last European land before a lot of Atlantic.
EINN.av: Foynes boats from 1937. Yankee Clipper 9 July 1939. Shannon land 1942–45. Duty-free airport 1947.
EINN.line: Shannon. Flying boats at Foynes, then the first duty-free airport on earth.
EINN.why: Westbound, this is where fuel math gets serious.

EBBR.name: Brussels
EBBR.av: SNETA Brussels–Croydon 25 May 1920. Zaventem terminal 5 July 1958.
EBBR.line: Brussels. Sabena's grandparents flew this field to Croydon in 1920.
EBBR.why: Flat land. Drift is a number.
